method: Matched parent/full, per-seed comparisons across effective current-delivered stress. Legacy cases excluded.

validation.meaning: Only finished pairs with passing per-case numerical/adapter checks and matching geometry, histories, and time windows enter; weak coherent returns may leave closure unavailable. This is not electromagnetic, physical, or GMF validation.

figures.title: Cho effect · ak 0.15, mono, stress 0°
figures.caption: Held-out band-variance and coherent-velocity differences, using matched parent/full histories. Each seed is a separate line; two seeds are not a confidence interval. Gray crosses mark unavailable estimates. A finite, resolved band variance can be reported even when coherent Doppler or an MTF fit is too weak.

figures.title: Modulation response · ak 0.15, mono, stress 0°
figures.caption: Training-interval numerical m_r and m_i at fixed sea-state settings; solid curves include Cho, dashed curves are parent-only. Colors identify individual seeds. The horizontal coordinate is effective current-stress friction velocity squared, not atmospheric stress or U10. Missing coefficients remain masked.

highlights: 8 of 20 new-case parent/full pairs are available; 12 unfinished, 0 missing paired analyses, 0 excluded by checks.
Separate seed curves retain realization differences; no two-seed confidence estimate is claimed.
limitations: Effective stress is tau_c = rho_water u*,c²; no direct aerodynamic parent/Cho growth and no U10 mapping.
Only matching reference/actual steepness, stress direction, sea state, duration, radar geometry, and fit/test windows are connected across stress. Each seed remains separate.
Parent/full differences include interference in the coherent scattering response; a signed difference is not a negative absolute power.
Bragg-band variance is an uncalibrated geometric roughness proxy; coherent Doppler retains the parent-coordinate-motion limitations of each case.
Unfinished cases and invalid directional measurements are not assigned zero. Scientific conclusions remain preliminary.
